clue.text: Volume of trade passes through here!

definitions.text: Volume of trade passes through here!

blocks.clueFragment: Volume of trade passes through here!
blocks.note: surface reading: a busy place where lots of business is done
setter's reading: volume means a book, so this is the place that trades in volumes

explanation.surface: A boast about a busy shop where a great deal of commerce goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' reads as quantity, but it means a book: the place where books are traded.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookshop is a retail store where books, or volumes, are bought and sold.

clue.text: Heartless country's controlled messaging

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word is taken out

explanation.surface: A nation's propaganda is described as lacking any compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the central A of SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of news by press officers to manage public opinion.

clue.text: Let sir get drunk with lots of wine?

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger about and lose their order

explanation.surface: Someone invites a gentleman to get drunk on plenty of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: litres measure any liquid, wine included.
explanation.definitionFit: Litres are metric units of liquid volume, so several of them make a generous quantity of wine.

clue.text: Female party has high point with intrusion of two knights

indicators.note: an intrusion pushes into something, so these letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight, twice

explanation.surface: A women's celebration peaks when a couple of knights gatecrash it.
explanation.walkthrough: N rather than K is used for knight in chess notation, since K is the king. A hen night is the British name for a bride's party before her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a celebration for a bride-to-be attended by her female friends.

clue.text: Mrs Churchill and Mr Attlee in England's capital

indicators.note: a capital letter heads the word, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Clement Attlee, post-war Labour Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Two political spouses or leaders together in London, England's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placing instruction but is simply the letters IN. Clementine was Winston Churchill's wife; Clement Attlee was the Labour Prime Minister who defeated him in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Clementine Churchill was the wife of Winston Churchill, so her first name serves for Mrs Churchill.

clue.text: Gritty bits one's found at end of street

indicators.note: found at the end means placed after the following word in the build

explanation.surface: Someone discovers grit lying at the far end of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Stones are small hard pieces of rock, the kind of gritty fragments found underfoot.

clue.text: Firm policy when politician's put in an hour of prayer!

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside the other letters

explanation.surface: A company's policy turns into prayer once an MP gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as an adjective describing the policy, but it is a noun for a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Compline is the last of the canonical hours, the church's set times for daily prayer, said before bed.

clue.text: Station American in establishment near Slough

indicators.note: one thing is in another, so these letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: Eton College, beside the town of Slough

explanation.surface: An American is stationed at a school near Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: Euston is a main-line railway terminus in London. Eton is a famous boarding school across the river from Slough.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of London's principal railway stations.

clue.text: Old stone artefact, one displayed in new hotel

indicators.note: something displayed in a case sits inside it
new makes the following word into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An ancient flint tool goes on show in a newly opened hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An eolith is a crudely chipped flint once thought to be among the earliest human tools.

clue.text: Hide king wearing something wicked

indicators.note: the thing worn wraps around the wearer, so one word goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A monarch disguises himself in something sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but it is the noun, an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is the skin of an animal, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Not all are 'sent' men, terrible bitterness being shown

indicators.note: only part of the following run of words is used, so the solution sits within them

blocks.note: the letters run across these words, dropping the opening A and the end of the last

explanation.surface: Bitterness arises because some men, though deemed sent, behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is a lasting indignation at being treated unfairly, the same feeling as bitterness.

clue.text: Pals keeping quiet may be fools

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

blocks.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet

explanation.surface: Friends who stay silent might be idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is a foolish or easily duped person, a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Daisy, maiden to maintain religious procedure

blocks.note: M for maiden, a cricket over with no runs
to maintain a view is to argue it

explanation.surface: A young woman called Daisy upholds a church ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' reads as a girl's name but is the flower. M stands for maiden in cricket scoring, an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A marguerite is a type of large white daisy, so it is an example of the flower.

clue.text: Musician roasting when playing

indicators.note: playing about with something rearranges it

explanation.surface: A performer gets hot under the lights while at the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist plays the organ, so is a particular kind of musician.

clue.text: Dad about to hug a daughter in ceremonial event?

indicators.note: a hug wraps around someone, so the next letters go inside

explanation.surface: A father embraces his daughter at a formal occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a formal procession, often military, put on as a ceremony.

clue.text: Detective longed to be apart

explanation.surface: A detective yearned for separation from the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detached stands separate, set apart from what is around it.

clue.text: A judicial procedure in court

definitions.note: adjective: relating to an atrium, a court or hall

explanation.surface: A legal case is being heard before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in court' seems to continue the legal story, but it defines: an atrium is a central court, so atrial means relating to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrial is the adjective from atrium, an open central courtyard or hall in a Roman house or modern building.

clue.text: Europeans in surprisingly valiant struggle initially

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the word turns out unexpectedly, in a new order
initially points to only the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: People from Europe put up an unexpectedly brave fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvians are citizens of Latvia, a Baltic state, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: Snakes less happy, beginning to slide to the bottom

indicators.text: beginning to slide to the bottom
indicators.note: the opening letter slips from the front down to the end of the word, a down clue's bottom

explanation.surface: Snakes become more miserable as they slip to the foot of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first S of SADDER to the end; in a down clue the end is the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Adders are vipers, the only venomous snakes native to Britain.

clue.text: Pipe buried in a garden plot must be taken away

indicators.note: buried in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a plus bed, a garden plot

explanation.surface: A pipe found buried in a garden must be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off by force, so abducted means taken away.

clue.text: Bishop, he turned up to lead ancient see

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top
leading means going in front of the next part

explanation.surface: A bishop arrives to take charge of an ancient diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese, fitting the church surface, but it is the verb, to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old imperative meaning look at, the same as the command see.

clue.text: Deal with enemy finally to effect this?

definitions.text: Deal with enemy finally to effect this?

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to treat with someone is to negotiate

explanation.surface: Negotiating with a foe at last to bring about a peace settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: one treats with the enemy to achieve a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, the deal that negotiations with a foe aim to produce.

clue.text: Sample provided by plant after short time

indicators.note: after places the second part behind the first

blocks.note: T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A small trial portion comes from a plant after a brief wait.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample given to try something out.

clue.text: Letters maybe from people in play?

blocks.note: first meaning: written symbols such as letters
second meaning: the figures in a drama

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests correspondence from actors; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Characters are both written symbols, of which letters are an example, and the roles in a play or story.

clue.text: Asian country lacking a prominent feature?

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the letter to be taken away

explanation.surface: An Asian nation is said to have no notable characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' is a facial feature; the question mark flags that a chin juts out literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is a feature of the face that sticks out at the front, hence prominent.

clue.text: Endearing sort of accent, setting leader apart

indicators.note: setting the leader aside removes the front letter of the word

blocks.note: the acute accent, as in café

explanation.surface: A charming way of speaking stands out from those of the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' suggests a voice, but it is a mark over a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive in a sweet way, so it is a synonym of endearing.

clue.text: Silly person, the ambassador in dress

blocks.note: a British word for a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish diplomat turns up in a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in dress' reads as wearing a dress, but 'dress' is the verb defining the answer and 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to put clothes on them, the same as to dress them.

clue.text: Somehow detecting coin in grass

indicators.note: one thing is in another, so these letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: to grass or sing is to inform on someone to the police

explanation.surface: Someone spots a coin lying in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like a lawn, but it is British slang for informing, which is also to sing. The first word qualifies the definition: scenting is detecting by one particular means, smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenting is detecting something by its smell, one way among many of detecting.
